question: What is the volume of a hemisphere with radius 2.8 cm? { (Use} left.pi=(22)/(7)) (Rounded up to three places of decimal).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a hemisphere, apply the direct formula: Volume = 2/3 × π × r³

Substitute r = 2.8 cm: V = 2/3 × 22/7 × (2.8)³

V = 44/21 × 21.952 = 965.888 ÷ 21

V ≈ 45.9946... cm³

Rounding to three decimal places gives 45.995 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.995 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the hemisphere (r) = 2.8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hemisphere (V) = 2/3 × π × r³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1bb231dcce8606af7b8ccf088f6f3e54f7764c62a08884bfeb286551169c94da.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ V = 2/3 × 22/7 × (2.8)³

⇒ V = 44/21 × (2.8 × 2.8 × 2.8)

⇒ V = 44/21 × 21.952

⇒ V = 965.888 ÷ 21

⇒ V = 45.99466... cm³

⇒ Rounding to three decimal places, V = 45.995 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 45.995 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Hemisphere Surface Areas

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr² | Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr²

Complete Sphere

Volume = 4/3 × πr³ | Surface Area = 4πr²

Cylinder

Volume = πr²h | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h)

Cone

Volume = 1/3 × πr²h | Curved Surface Area = πrl (where slant height l = √(r² + h²))
